nom: Sun Bum Mineral Sunscreen Face Tint SPF 30

segments.oily: Oily-skin reviewers are split: several say it mattifies well and controls shine all day, but others report it never fully sets, slides off, or turns greasy after a few hours.
segments.dry: Dry-skin reviewers most often report the product pilled, clung to dry patches, or left skin very dry and tight, though a couple describe it as non-drying and comfortable when layered over moisturizer.
segments.combination: Combination-skin reviewers report the sunscreen became patchy and heavily drying within days of use.
segments.sensitive: Sensitive-skin reviewers largely praise it for causing no irritation, stinging, or breakouts, though a few with sensitive/acne-prone skin still report whiteheads or a rash-like reaction.
segments.mature: Mature-skin reviewers describe it as a comfortable, non-drying primer-like sunscreen that blurs imperfections without emphasizing wrinkles or dryness.

concerns.aging: Reviewers using it on mature skin say it blurs fine lines and imperfections gently without irritation; one reviewer with no wrinkles felt it made her skin look temporarily wrinkly due to pilling.
concerns.dehydration: Multiple reviewers report the product made their skin very dry, tight, or patchy within a day or two, though a few describe it as moisturizing and non-drying, especially when worn over a hydrating base.
concerns.redness: Several reviewers with rosacea or general redness say it visibly reduces redness and feels gentle; no dissenting reports of increased redness were found.
concerns.barrier: No specific reviewer commentary on barrier function beyond general dryness/irritation already captured under dehydration.
concerns.spots: One reviewer with hyperpigmentation-prone, deeper skin found the tint left a dead, ashy, undertaker-like cast rather than helping with dark spots.
concerns.blemishes: Most acne-prone reviewers report no breakouts and even improved makeup wear over blemishes; three others explicitly describe new whiteheads or cystic-like pimples after use.
concerns.oiliness: Oily-skin reviewers are divided: many report a lasting matte, non-greasy finish, while others say it stays greasy, doesn't set, or becomes oily partway through the day.

aspects.libelle: White cast on fair to deep skin
Minimal visible tint versus packaging claim
Good value for a mineral sunscreen

extraits.texte: It worked okay for a bit, but after a couple of days it started to become patchy, drying out my skin HEAVILY and that means something especially bc I have oily/combination skin. You have to mix it constantly, and if you don't mix it long enough when you open it liquid starts pouring out like crazy

extraits.titre: Gave me pimples but it's still ok
extraits.texte: I used this entire tube… But I wont be repurchasing. While it didnt leave a cast on my skin and had a nice smoothing quality and tint when applied, it caused me to breakout. It would cause these little whiteheads to form all over my face. They were easy enough to get rid of but such a shame because I think this product has a lot of pros, I just have really sensitive skin and acne so it is not for me.

I really wanted to love this product because it is very silky and comfortable, and the tint is just enough to disappear on my skin. The only problem is I have quite oily skin and this product never fully sets down on me. It can be hours later and I touch my face and it comes right off. I have tried powdering my face which helped a little, but I think I'm going to use the rest of it as a body SPF. If you are very oily like me, I can't recommend this one but maybe give the Australian Gold tinted SPF50 a try.

extraits.titre: Think of it as a "Non Drying Primer with Sunscreen"
extraits.texte: I have mature, light-medium, neutral undertone skin with lots of imperfections. I am most comfortable with a tinted moisturizer, primer and blush. Most sunscreens feel heavy on my skin; ditto with foundations. And anything that feels thick or heavy also makes me itch. In an effort to avoid the constant scratching, I decided to use only mineral based sunscreen products. I've tried everything from CeraVe to Drunk Elephant and La Roche Pose to Elta, yet nothing seems to be what I can wear all day comfortably. I tried this for the first time yesterday and I was impressed! I applied a light moisturizer to my clean face, and then, following other's comments, shook the tube really well, and applied the dermatologist-recommended 1/2 teaspoon. Although it felt like a lot, it was lightweight, the color blended in easily, it soaked in quickly, and did a great job of serving as a primer. It is definitely a matte finish. I let it dry, applied concealer and blush over it, and left the house. Sixteen hours later, it was still intact, none had accumulated in my "creases" or under my eyes, and I hadn't scratched my face at all. It came off easily with one shot of my regular salicylic acid face wash and my skin felt fine. I did the whole thing again today, and having just washed it off, there are no signs of irritation, outbreaks, extra dryness, excessive oil, etc. I am purchasing another tube today because I can't believe this is so effective for me and it is at this price point. extraits.titre: My HG for a few years now.
extraits.texte: Over the years I've realized my skin is just not very compatible with chemical SPF so I've had to find a new mineral daily driver. I tried soooooo many from low high end, and I've landed on this one!! I have super fair, Irish freckly, sensitive skin, so most tinted SPF is too dark/orange for me- ESPECIALLY upon reapplication. This one is literally perfect, I use it in place on place of foundation now bc the finish is so nice. No white cast, no orange cast (lol), unscented, it has the perfect finish- light pore filling, matte finish but doesn't dry me out. I don't have to use a powder over this which makes reapplication sooo easy (wish I remembered this more, but I'm bad about reapplying) This might be too light for darker skin tones, I wish it had a few color options like the Australian Gold, but that one is way too matte, drying, scented, and burns my eyes.

extraits.titre: Works for my sensitive, acne prone skin
extraits.texte: I'm always on the hunt for a good sunscreen with no fragrance or anything possibly irritating due to my skin being very acne prone. I got this one after seeing some good reviews on here and on YouTube. It has really surprised me how well it has worked for me, no irritation, no break outs and actually has made my makeup go on very smoothly and look better throughout the day. The texture took some getting used to, it feels like a mousse/silicone primer, but not overly silicone feeling. I'm Very impressed and glad I found a spf that doesn't break me out!

I've used tinited sunscreen before, but this stuff made me look like a zombie. I looked like the undertaker did my make-up. If I died, this would be the complexion of my skin. If you have pigmentation (read - black / brown skin tone), SAVE your money! I'm definitely returning. No wonder it was by one, get one 40% off … they are trying to give it away!
